Updated September 2026
Index Work Record Stories About

Zen Aegis

Venture · Technology

Zen Aegis is an AI transformation partner in Phoenix, Arizona, founded in 2023 and led by Robby Prochnow. It builds and operates custom AI agent systems inside client businesses and runs its own company on the same infrastructure.

Wiki/Zen Aegis

What Zen Aegis is

Zen Aegis began in 2023 as a consulting business, grew into a fractional leadership firm and is now an AI transformation partner. It builds custom AI agent systems inside a client’s business, operates them, and stays embedded until the results are real. It runs its own company on the same infrastructure it deploys for clients.

Robby Prochnow founded it and leads it. Before Zen Aegis he spent more than a decade running technology businesses inside large distributors and a global internet-services company; his record is on his page.

How it works

A working prototype first. The signature offer is a free working prototype built on the client’s own workflow before the client pays. The company’s own line for it: “We’ll build it before you buy it.”

Self-hosted, one client per boundary. Nothing about a client’s prompts, outputs, credentials or content leaves the boundary. Each client is isolated at the infrastructure layer, with its own host, its own secrets vault, its own tracing and its own set of tool servers. See Guardrails for a self-hosted agent platform and the story Keeping the prompts inside the walls.

Agent teams with a person at the gate. Zen Aegis runs teams of named agents, each with its own lane. Work that has to come out the same way every time runs as a fixed workflow; agents do the reasoning; a person approves before anything is sent. Every agent session is saved to a private, versioned record that the next session reads first. No AI claim ships without a source that can be checked live.

The standard. Everything it builds is held to five commitments: governed, secured, compounding, watched and measured. On compliance it says exactly this and no more: it builds HIPAA-compliant systems, runs on ISO 27001-certified infrastructure and builds to GDPR practice.

Products

  • Foyer Hall: a white-label client portal and data room with signatures, files, invoices and an agent interface. Common Ground’s first client room runs on it.
  • Slipstream: a search and AI-visibility workspace that pairs Common Ground’s audit method with an automated scoring and monitoring engine.
  • Aegis Lens: a diagnostic that runs inside a client’s environment, collects the facts itself and ranks findings with evidence. A prototype on sample data, ready to show.
  • Grant Match AI: a public grant-matching engine for nonprofits.
  • Acquire Desk: buy-side deal origination, live for a business brokerage.
  • Everstead: a personal development app for web and mobile, labeled a prototype. It writes a custom meditation of up to 20 minutes, ready to play within seconds, and offers a council of coaches for training, mindfulness and work.
  • An agent skill library of 89 versioned, owner-attributed, security-reviewed skills, a reporting layer over its core data, a dashboard for running an agent workforce, and an agency back office still at prototype.

Zen Aegis is also building a standalone AI agent platform, not yet shipping. Common Ground’s own client tool set is described on the Kinwork page.

How it came into Common Ground

Robby Prochnow met the Common Ground partners in March 2026 and started the way he starts with any client: an audit of each partner’s technology, delivered in April with recorded walkthroughs. Since May 2026 he has run technology for the group. Common Ground’s first client room runs on Foyer Hall, Slipstream pairs the group’s search method with his platform, and the group is moving its own work onto the Zen Aegis agent team. Work Zen Aegis did for clients before and alongside Common Ground is listed below by description, never by client name: that is the company’s standing rule.

Work on record

Aegis LensAegis Lens is a Zen Aegis prototype that runs inside a client's environment, collects the facts a questionnaire would ask for, ranks what it finds with evidence and holds every deliverable for a person's approval.Technology · 2026 Agent team for a multi-market business brokerageFive named agents on dedicated, isolated infrastructure took over inbox triage and buy-side origination for a multi-market business brokerage, reclaiming 71.3 inbox hours in seven days.Technology · 2026 Cascade IRWithin about a day of a posting for investor-deck automation, Zen Aegis built a working engine that refreshes approved investor decks in place from one data layer, with 46 fields wired to source and no change to the design.Technology · 2026 Email operations that learn from correctionsAn email triage system Zen Aegis runs for itself and for other organizations, where every human correction can become a permanent rule: 9,803 emails triaged from April to August 2026 and {{fact:zen-aegis.34-7-hours}} a week reclaimed.Technology · 2026 Expert program for an online education companyA complete expert program for an online education company, 17 modules and more than 80 lessons on a 10-week path, delivered live inside the first month.Technology · 2026 Four apps in one dayZen Aegis built four working apps live in a single day as a public demonstration, including a commercial insurance quoting tool and a credit intelligence tool, and separately had an autonomous agent build and compare two rapid-development platforms.Technology · 2026 Foyer HallFoyer Hall is Zen Aegis's white-label client portal and data room. Common Ground moved its first client room onto it in late September 2026, and its first invoice became payable by bank or card on October 6.Technology · 2026 Go-to-market build for a B2B SaaS companyPositioning, a new site, a blog system, four phases of search work, outreach and paid traffic for a B2B SaaS company, run as one retainer: 6,048 sessions in {{fact:zen-aegis.130-days}}.Technology · 2026 Grant Match AIA public, open-repository grant discovery engine for nonprofits that scores each funder on six factors, with rules doing the arithmetic and a model doing only the judgment calls.Technology · 2026 Guardrails for a self-hosted agent platformThe controls Zen Aegis built into its own agent platform: a gate that blocks any AI claim without a live source, per-agent secrets, database-enforced tenancy, a ban on agents checking their own work, and a security memo client teams can review.Technology · 2026 Lifted Trucks mission controlA collective Common Ground proof of concept for Lifted Trucks, a prospective client: a working six-screen demo of what a mission control for multi-state inventory could look like, shipped May 21, 2026.Technology · 2026 Medical-record review for an in-house legal teamZen Aegis automated the gathering, summarizing and delivery of medical records for an in-house legal team; one case that historically cost about {{fact:zen-aegis.usd-75-000}} came in at a fraction of the cost in one-tenth of the time.Technology · 2025 to 2026 Search build for an independent financial advisory practiceA publishing system and a local landing page for an independent financial advisory practice ranked second in organic search for a competitive metro retirement-planning keyword within the first week, with no ad spend.Technology · 2026 Sites for a strategy firm, a youth sports nonprofit and a family foundationThree live client builds: a rebuilt homepage and development standard for a strategy consulting firm, a site with online registration for a youth sports nonprofit, and a hosted site for a family foundation.Technology · 2026 Slipstream scoring engineSlipstream's automated engine scores how a site shows up in search and AI answers. Before it was trusted it was run against an expert's hand audit of ten sites and agreed {{fact:zen-aegis.92-8-percent}} of the time with no factual conflicts.Technology · 2026

Decisions on record

Collecting the facts instead of asking for themThe usual first step in a technology engagement is a long questionnaire.Insider truth Building it instead of pitching itIn July 2026 a posting asked for someone to automate investor materials: keep the decks current from the numbers without breaking the approved design.Strong opinion Four apps in one day, built where people could watchEvery firm selling AI work says it builds fast.Origin Two hours to fix the first client invoiceIn late September 2026 Zen Aegis asked Common Ground to put a real client into Foyer Hall, its white-label client portal.High-stakes save A gate that will not let an unsourced claim out the doorAI agents write fluently whether or not they are right.Standing on principle Keeping the prompts inside the wallsThe easy way to build AI systems for clients is to put every client on one shared stack and send everything through outside services.Standing on principle No savings number before the baselineWhen Common Ground scoped a technology engagement for a private-equity-backed dental group in August 2026, Robby Prochnow wrote the 90-day technology plan.The honest call Testing the engine against an expert before trusting its scoresBy August 2026 Zen Aegis had an automated engine that scored how a website shows up in search and in AI answers: 53 checks in four weighted categories, with the evidence for every result stored next to it.Teaching moment
